description:
FILED s450v (Opus round 9 agent V), the residue of #521.  LOUD (a `;; PARSE
ERROR` drop with the compiler's own message), never silent.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3):

    my $x = "mAn"; $x =~ s/A/${\ "L\"Q"}/; print "$x\n";
        perl  mL"Qn
        PCL   PCL: statement dropped ... PCL internal: s/// replacement did not
              lower as a dq string: '${\ "L\"Q"}'

    (The same block in a real dq string, `"X${\ \"L\\\"Q\"}Y"`, is the same
    shape and also drops.)

CAUSE: a LOSSY round trip.  `_gen_interp_replacement` wraps the replacement in a
manufactured `"..."` token, escaping EVERY `"` with `s/"/\\"/g` -- including one
that was ALREADY escaped in the source.  `${\ "L\"Q"}` becomes
`${\ \"L\\"Q\"}`, and s450v's `_undelimit` (which undoes exactly one `\"` per
escape and preserves `\\` pairs, matching perl -- see #521) then reads
`${\ "L\\"Q"}`, which PPI cannot parse.  Escaping only the UNESCAPED quotes does
not help either: the source's own `\"` means a literal `"` at the REPLACEMENT
level, and inside a `${...}` block it is a `"` in the block's own string, so the
two levels genuinely disagree about one character.

SHAPE OF A FIX: stop the round trip for the block -- either compile the block's
guts from the RAW replacement text (its span is known: the scanner's expr_span)
instead of re-escaping the whole replacement into a dq token, or make the
manufactured token carry the raw text with a delimiter that does not occur in
it.  The first is the rule-11 direction: the guts are already a fragment the
pipeline knows how to compile.

BAR: the two spellings above plus `${\ q(L"Q)}` (works today) vs perl; a row in
Pl/t/regexp-subst-01.t beside the s450v #521 rows.
subject: LOUD DROP: an ESCAPED QUOTE inside a `${ ... }` block in an s/// replacement -- `s/A/${\ "L\"Q"}/` drops the statement
